key_insight: An interpretable machine-learning framework predicts static molten chloride corrosion, with salt preparation emerging as the dominant model descriptor.
engineering_relevance: The framework could support alloy and salt-condition screening by estimating corrosion rates alongside prediction uncertainty.
method: Compiled 291 literature-reported static molten chloride corrosion experiments.
Introduced a graded Chloride Salt Preparation Index (CSPI) capturing salt treatment, atmosphere control, and pre-exposure impurity condition.
Used a blended tree-based ensemble, sensitivity and SHAP analyses, and conformal prediction intervals.
evidence_signal: The ensemble achieved cross-validated R² = 0.85 and MAE = 0.41 mg cm⁻² day⁻¹; the abstract reports well-calibrated prediction intervals.
watch_item: Results are based on static literature tests; transfer to flowing systems or conditions outside the dataset requires validation.
paper_title: Data-Driven Modeling of Molten Chloride Corrosion Using Static Test Data
